750	## 5. Containers (round 1)
751	
752	Every file here is a deployment artifact. The lead reviews each one before it is applied or merged (`deployment.md`). Base images are pinned to the exact versions in § 13.1. The `api` and `web` images are tagged `${GIT_SHA:-local}`, never `latest`.
753	
754	### 5.1 Backend `Dockerfile` (multi-stage, uv, non-root)
755	
756	Following [uv's Docker guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/docker/):
757	
758	```dockerfile
759	FROM python:3.14.8-slim-trixie AS build
760	COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.23 /uv /bin/uv
761	ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=0
762	WORKDIR /app
763	RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
764	    --mount=type=bind,source=uv.lock,target=uv.lock \
765	    --mount=type=bind,source=pyproject.toml,target=pyproject.toml \
766	    uv sync --locked --no-install-project --no-dev          # dependency layer, cached
767	COPY . .
768	RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv uv sync --locked --no-dev --no-editable
769	
770	FROM python:3.14.8-slim-trixie
771	RUN groupadd --system --gid 10001 app && useradd --system --uid 10001 --gid app --no-create-home app
772	WORKDIR /app
773	COPY --from=build --chown=app:app /app/.venv /app/.venv
774	COPY --chown=app:app app ./app
775	COPY --chown=app:app alembic ./alembic
776	COPY --chown=app:app alembic.ini ./
777	ENV PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH" PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
778	USER 10001
779	EXPOSE 8000
780	CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:create_app", "--factory", …the flags in § 3.11.1]
781	```
782	
783	`.dockerignore`: `.venv`, `tests`, `.pytest_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.coverage`, `htmlcov`, `__pycache__`.
784	
785	### 5.2 Frontend `Dockerfile` (build, then unprivileged nginx)
786	
787	```dockerfile
788	FROM node:24.21.0-alpine3.24 AS build
789	WORKDIR /app
790	COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
791	RUN npm ci
792	COPY . .
793	RUN npm run build
794	
795	FROM nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.30.6-alpine3.24   # listens on 8080, runs as uid 101
796	COPY nginx.conf /etc/nginx/nginx.conf                 # replaces the main config, so worker_processes is ours
797	COPY --from=build /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
798	EXPOSE 8080
799	```
800	
801	nginx 1.30.6 is the stable branch's security release (§ 13.1). `server … resolve` has been in open-source nginx since 1.27.3. `.dockerignore`: `node_modules`, `dist`, `coverage`, `design`, `*.test.*`, `src/test`.
802	
803	### 5.3 `frontend/nginx.conf`
804	
805	The file replaces the image's main `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf`, because `worker_processes` is only valid in the main context, not in a `conf.d/` include.
806	
807	```nginx
808	worker_processes 2;                                    # pinned: the image's "auto" means one per CPU
809	pid /tmp/nginx.pid;                                    # the unprivileged image writes only to /tmp
810	events { worker_connections 4096; }                    # each proxied request holds 2 connections
811	
812	http {
813	include mime.types;
814	access_log /dev/stdout; error_log /dev/stderr warn;
815	client_body_temp_path /tmp/client_temp; proxy_temp_path /tmp/proxy_temp;
816	fastcgi_temp_path /tmp/fastcgi_temp; uwsgi_temp_path /tmp/uwsgi_temp; scgi_temp_path /tmp/scgi_temp;
817	
818	resolver 127.0.0.11 valid=10s ipv6=off;               # Docker's DNS; replicas can change IPs
819	map $http_x_request_id $req_id { default $http_x_request_id; "" $request_id; }
820	
821	upstream api {
822	  zone api 64k;
823	  server api:8000 resolve;                             # both replicas, round-robin
824	  keepalive 16;                                        # no "local": both /api locations share one cache per worker
825	  keepalive_timeout 60s;                               # shorter than uvicorn's 75 s
826	}
827	
828	server {
829	  listen 8080;
830	  server_tokens off;
831	  client_max_body_size 64k;                            # D13
832	  root /usr/share/nginx/html;
833	
834	  # Security headers. Repeated in each location that sets its own, because add_header does not inherit.
835	  set $csp "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'";
836	  add_header Content-Security-Policy $csp always;
837	  add_header X-Content-Type-Options nosniff always;
838	  add_header Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin always;
839	  add_header X-Frame-Options DENY always;
840	  add_header Permissions-Policy "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()" always;
841	  add_header Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy same-origin always;
842	
843	  location = /livez  { return 404; }                   # D19: probes are not routed
844	  location = /readyz { return 404; }
845	
846	  location /api/ {
847	    proxy_pass http://api;                             # HTTP/1.1 and no Connection header are defaults since 1.29.7
848	    proxy_set_header Host $host;
849	    proxy_set_header X-Request-ID $req_id;
850	    proxy_read_timeout 30s;
851	    # + the security headers
852	  }
853	  location = /api/docs { proxy_pass http://api; …; add_header Content-Security-Policy "<docs CSP>" always; … }   # (Q-13)
854	  location /assets/ { add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"; … }
855	  location / { try_files $uri /index.html; add_header Cache-Control "no-cache"; … }   # SPA fallback
856	}
857	}
858	```
859	
860	**Keep-alive arithmetic.** Since nginx 1.29.7 upstream keep-alive is on by default as `keepalive 32 local`, where `local` stops connections being reused across locations ([nginx upstream: keepalive](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_upstream_module.html#keepalive)). The explicit `keepalive 16` without `local` sets the cap and lets `/api/` and `/api/docs` share one cache. `keepalive 16` caps the *idle* upstream connections each worker caches, shared across every server in the group ([nginx upstream](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_upstream_module.html#keepalive)). With 2 workers, at most 2 × 16 = **32 idle connections** exist in total. That is about 16 per replica when spread evenly, and 32 in the worst case where one replica holds them all. Against uvicorn's `--limit-concurrency 200`, at least 168 slots stay free for requests in flight on each replica. With the image's default `auto` on a 10-core Mac it would have been 10 × 16 = 160 idle connections, leaving as few as 40. `worker_connections 4096` gives 8,192 connections in total, about 4,000 proxied requests at once, so nginx is not the bottleneck in the stepped run's 1,000-user step.
861	
862	- `resolve` with a shared `zone` re-resolves `api` as replicas come and go ([nginx upstream](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_upstream_module.html)).
863	- `proxy_next_upstream` keeps its default. nginx does not retry non-idempotent requests on another replica.
864	- The `/api/docs` CSP allows the Swagger UI's CDN script and style and its inline start-up script. It applies to that one path only.
865	- gzip is on for JS, CSS and JSON.
866	
867	### 5.4 `docker-compose.yml`
868	
869	| Service | Image or build | Depends on | Healthcheck | Notes |
870	|---|---|---|---|---|
871	| `db` | `postgres:18.6-alpine3.24` | | `pg_isready -U $$POSTGRES_USER -d $$POSTGRES_DB`, every 5 s, 10 retries, start period 10 s | Volume `pgdata` mounted at **`/var/lib/postgresql`**. From 18 the image keeps `PGDATA` at `/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker` beneath it; a mount at the old `/var/lib/postgresql/data` would lose the data when the container is re-created ([image docs](https://hub.docker.com/_/postgres)). No published port. |
872	| `migrate` | build `./backend`, image `todo-api:${GIT_SHA:-local}` | `db: service_healthy` | none (one-shot; its exit code is the signal) | `command: ["alembic", "upgrade", "head"]`, `restart: "no"`, only `DATABASE_URL` |
873	| `api` | same build and image | `migrate: service_completed_successfully`, `db: service_healthy` ([depends_on conditions](https://docs.docker.com/reference/compose-file/services/#depends_on)) | `python -c "urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/readyz', timeout=2)"`, every 5 s | `deploy.replicas: 2`, `expose: ["8000"]`, `stop_grace_period: 25s`, the five app env vars |
874	| `web` | build `./frontend`, image `todo-web:${GIT_SHA:-local}` | `api: service_healthy` | `wget -q --spider http://127.0.0.1:8080/` | `ports: ["127.0.0.1:8080:8080"]`, the only published port |
875	| `k6` | `grafana/k6:2.3.0` | `web: service_healthy` | none (one-shot) | `profiles: ["load"]`. Mounts `./load/k6:/scripts:ro` and `./load/results:/results`. `BASE_URL=http://web:8080`, `APP_ORIGIN`, `VUS`, `HOLD`. |
876	| `test-db` | `postgres:18.6-alpine3.24` | | `pg_isready` | `profiles: ["test"]`. `127.0.0.1:55432:5432`, `tmpfs` at `/var/lib/postgresql` (the same 18 data path), `-c fsync=off -c synchronous_commit=off -c full_page_writes=off`, throwaway credentials. For local backend test runs only **(Q-5)**. |
877	
878	Hardening on `api`, `migrate` and `web`: `read_only: true`, `tmpfs: [/tmp]`, `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]`. `DATABASE_URL` is built in the file: `postgresql+asyncpg://${POSTGRES_USER:?}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?}@db:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:?}`. `migrate` and `api` declare the same build; BuildKit's cache makes the second build a no-op.
879	
880	Commands: `docker compose up --build --wait` (the stack); `docker compose --profile test up -d test-db` (backend tests); `docker compose --profile load run --rm k6 run /scripts/journey.js` (load).
881	
882	---
883	
884	## 6. Test plan

## 5. Containers (round 1)

### 5.1 Backend `Dockerfile` (multi-stage, uv, non-root)

Following [uv's Docker guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/docker/):

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.14.8-slim-trixie AS build
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.23 /uv /bin/uv
ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=0
WORKDIR /app
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    --mount=type=bind,source=uv.lock,target=uv.lock \
    --mount=type=bind,source=pyproject.toml,target=pyproject.toml \
    uv sync --locked --no-install-project --no-dev          # dependency layer, cached
COPY . .
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv uv sync --locked --no-dev --no-editable

FROM python:3.14.8-slim-trixie
RUN groupadd --system --gid 10001 app && useradd --system --uid 10001 --gid app --no-create-home app
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build --chown=app:app /app/.venv /app/.venv
COPY --chown=app:app app ./app
COPY --chown=app:app alembic ./alembic
COPY --chown=app:app alembic.ini ./
ENV PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH" PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
USER 10001
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:create_app", "--factory", …the flags in § 3.11.1]
```

`.dockerignore`: `.venv`, `tests`, `.pytest_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.coverage`, `htmlcov`, `__pycache__`.

### 5.2 Frontend `Dockerfile` (build, then unprivileged nginx)

```dockerfile
FROM node:24.21.0-alpine3.24 AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build
```

nginx 1.30.6 is the stable branch's security release (§ 13.1). `server … resolve` has been in open-source nginx since 1.27.3. `.dockerignore`: `node_modules`, `dist`, `coverage`, `design`, `*.test.*`, `src/test`.

### 5.3 `frontend/nginx.conf`

The file replaces the image's main `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf`, because `worker_processes` is only valid in the main context, not in a `conf.d/` include.

```nginx
worker_processes 2;                                    # pinned: the image's "auto" means one per CPU
pid /tmp/nginx.pid;                                    # the unprivileged image writes only to /tmp
events { worker_connections 4096; }                    # each proxied request holds 2 connections

http {
include mime.types;
access_log /dev/stdout; error_log /dev/stderr warn;
client_body_temp_path /tmp/client_temp; proxy_temp_path /tmp/proxy_temp;
fastcgi_temp_path /tmp/fastcgi_temp; uwsgi_temp_path /tmp/uwsgi_temp; scgi_temp_path /tmp/scgi_temp;

resolver 127.0.0.11 valid=10s ipv6=off;               # Docker's DNS; replicas can change IPs
map $http_x_request_id $req_id { default $http_x_request_id; "" $request_id; }

upstream api {
  zone api 64k;
  server api:8000 resolve;                             # both replicas, round-robin
  keepalive 16;                                        # no "local": both /api locations share one cache per worker
  keepalive_timeout 60s;                               # shorter than uvicorn's 75 s
}

server {
  listen 8080;
  server_tokens off;
  client_max_body_size 64k;                            # D13
  root /usr/share/nginx/html;

  # Security headers. Repeated in each location that sets its own, because add_header does not inherit.
  set $csp "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'";
  add_header Content-Security-Policy $csp always;
  add_header X-Content-Type-Options nosniff always;
  add_header Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin always;
  add_header X-Frame-Options DENY always;
  add_header Permissions-Policy "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()" always;
  add_header Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy same-origin always;

  location = /livez  { return 404; }                   # D19: probes are not routed
  location = /readyz { return 404; }

  location /api/ {
    proxy_pass http://api;                             # HTTP/1.1 and no Connection header are defaults since 1.29.7
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Request-ID $req_id;
    proxy_read_timeout 30s;
    # + the security headers
  }
  location = /api/docs { proxy_pass http://api; …; add_header Content-Security-Policy "<docs CSP>" always; … }   # (Q-13)
  location /assets/ { add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"; … }
  location / { try_files $uri /index.html; add_header Cache-Control "no-cache"; … }   # SPA fallback
}
}
```

**Keep-alive arithmetic.** Since nginx 1.29.7 upstream keep-alive is on by default as `keepalive 32 local`, where `local` stops connections being reused across locations ([nginx upstream: keepalive](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_upstream_module.html#keepalive)). The explicit `keepalive 16` without `local` sets the cap and lets `/api/` and `/api/docs` share one cache. `keepalive 16` caps the *idle* upstream connections each worker caches, shared across every server in the group ([nginx upstream](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_upstream_module.html#keepalive)). With 2 workers, at most 2 × 16 = **32 idle connections** exist in total. That is about 16 per replica when spread evenly, and 32 in the worst case where one replica holds them all. Against uvicorn's `--limit-concurrency 200`, at least 168 slots stay free for requests in flight on each replica. With the image's default `auto` on a 10-core Mac it would have been 10 × 16 = 160 idle connections, leaving as few as 40. `worker_connections 4096` gives 8,192 connections in total, about 4,000 proxied requests at once, so nginx is not the bottleneck in the stepped run's 1,000-user step.

- `resolve` with a shared `zone` re-resolves `api` as replicas come and go ([nginx upstream](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_upstream_module.html)).
- `proxy_next_upstream` keeps its default. nginx does not retry non-idempotent requests on another replica.
- The `/api/docs` CSP allows the Swagger UI's CDN script and style and its inline start-up script. It applies to that one path only.
- gzip is on for JS, CSS and JSON.

170	```python
171	def create_app(settings: Settings | None = None) -> FastAPI: ...
172	```
173	
174	- uvicorn runs it as `app.main:create_app --factory`, so nothing is built at import time and tests build their own app with their own settings.
175	- Order inside the factory: `configure_logging(settings)`, then `FastAPI(title="todo-app API", docs_url="/api/docs", openapi_url="/api/openapi.json", redoc_url=None, lifespan=lifespan)`, then store `settings` on `app.state`, then add `RequestContextMiddleware`, register the handlers (§ 3.4), and include `health_router` (root) and `api_router` (`/api/v1`).

180	
181	### 3.3 Middleware and the Origin guard
182	
183	**`RequestContextMiddleware`**, a pure ASGI middleware. A pure one, not `BaseHTTPMiddleware`, so it runs in the request's own task and context variables flow both ways ([Starlette: pure ASGI middleware](https://www.starlette.io/middleware/#pure-asgi-middleware)). For each HTTP request it:
184	
185	1. Takes `X-Request-ID` from the request when it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$`, and otherwise makes one (`uuid4().hex`). It sets the `request_id` context variable.
186	2. Wraps `send` so that `http.response.start` gets `X-Request-ID`, `X-Served-By: <socket.gethostname()>` and, for `/api/` paths, `Cache-Control: no-store`.
187	3. Times the request with `time.perf_counter()`. After the app returns, or raises, it logs one access line on logger `app.access`: `method`, `route` (the route template from `scope["route"].path`, or the raw path when nothing matched), `status`, `duration_ms`, plus `request_id` and `user_id` from the context. A successful `/livez` or `/readyz` is not logged, because probes every 5 s would drown the useful lines. A failed probe is logged.
188	4. On an exception escaping the app, it logs the access line with status 500 and re-raises. Starlette's outer `ServerErrorMiddleware` then calls the 500 handler (§ 3.4).
189	
190	`user_id` reaches the access line because `get_current_user` (an async dependency, so it runs in the same task) sets the `user_id` context variable. An integration test pins this (§ 6.3).
191	
192	**Origin guard**, `require_trusted_origin`. A dependency on `api_router`, so it covers every `/api/v1` route and raises a domain error that the handlers turn into the envelope (handlers never build bodies by hand).
193	
194	| Method | `Origin` header | Result |
195	|---|---|---|
196	| `GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS` | any | pass |
197	| `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` | equals `APP_ORIGIN` | pass |
198	| same | present and different, including the literal `null` | `ForbiddenOrigin` → 403 `forbidden_origin` |
199	| same | absent | pass **(Q-3)** |
200	
201	Browsers always attach `Origin` to a non-GET request, and send `null` rather than leaving it out when a policy hides it ([Fetch: append a request Origin header](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#append-a-request-origin-header)). 222	| Wrong email or password | `InvalidCredentials` | 401 | `invalid_credentials` | One message for unknown email and wrong password |

239	
240	```python

242	def create_sessionmaker(engine: AsyncEngine) -> async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]

```python
def create_app(settings: Settings | None = None) -> FastAPI: ...
```

1. Takes `X-Request-ID` from the request when it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$`, and otherwise makes one (`uuid4().hex`). It sets the `request_id` context variable.

3. Times the request with `time.perf_counter()`. 4. On an exception escaping the app, it logs the access line with status 500 and re-raises. Starlette's outer `ServerErrorMiddleware` then calls the 500 handler (§ 3.4).

`user_id` reaches the access line because `get_current_user` (an async dependency, so it runs in the same task) sets the `user_id` context variable. An integration test pins this (§ 6.3).

|---|---|---|

| `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` | equals `APP_ORIGIN` | pass |

- A thrown `TypeError` from `fetch` → `ApiError(status 0, code "network_error")`. An `AbortError` is rethrown untouched, so TanStack Query treats it as a cancellation.
- `ApiErrorCode` is an `as const` object with every code from § 3.4 plus the four derived ones.
- `declare module "@tanstack/react-query" { interface Register { defaultError: ApiError } }`, so every hook's `error` is typed ([TanStack: registering a global error](https://tanstack.com/query/v5/docs/framework/react/typescript#registering-a-global-error)).

`src/lib/api/tasks.ts`: `listTasks(q, signal)`, `getTask(id, signal)`, `createTask(input)`, `updateTask(id, patch, ifMatch?)`, `moveTask(id, afterId)`, `deleteTask(id)`. `src/lib/api/auth.ts`: `register(creds)`, `login(creds)`, `logout()`, `me(signal)`. `me` returns `User | null`: a 401 becomes `null`, so the global handler never fires for "not signed in yet".

### 4.3 Query keys and the query client

```ts
export const taskKeys = {
  all: ["tasks"] as const,
  lists: () => [...taskKeys.all, "list"] as const,
  list: (q: string) => [...taskKeys.lists(), { q }] as const,
  details: () => [...taskKeys.all, "detail"] as const,
  detail: (id: string) => [...taskKeys.details(), id] as const,
  mutations: { toggle: ["tasks", "toggle"], move: ["tasks", "move"], remove: ["tasks", "remove"], update: ["tasks", "update"], create: ["tasks", "create"] } as const,
};
export const authKeys = { me: ["auth", "me"] as const };
```

`createQueryClient({ onUnauthenticated }: { onUnauthenticated: () => void }): QueryClient`:

| Default | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `queries.staleTime` | `0` | Every focus or reconnect refetches what is on screen (D17, first layer) |
| `queries.refetchOnWindowFocus`, `refetchOnReconnect` | `true` (set explicitly) | D17. Also the TanStack default; stating it keeps the decision visible. |
| `queries.retry` | Up to 2 retries, only for `network_error` and `service_unavailable` | A 4xx will not change on retry |
| `mutations.retry` | `0` | Writes are not blindly repeated |
| `QueryCache.onError`, `MutationCache.onError` | `not_authenticated` → `queryClient.clear()` then `onUnauthenticated()`. Anything else → `console.error("[query] failed", { key: <resource name only>, status, code })` | Spec: a 401 is handled once, in the query client. Search terms and task text are never logged. `invalid_credentials` is not a session expiry and never redirects. |

`onUnauthenticated`, wired in `main.tsx`, calls `router.navigate("/sign-in?returnTo=" + encodeURIComponent(current path + search), { replace: true })`.

### 4.4 Hooks (`src/lib/query/tasks.ts`, `src/lib/query/auth.ts`)

| Hook | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `useTasks(q: string)` | `queryKey: taskKeys.list(q)`, `queryFn: ({ signal }) => listTasks(q, signal)`, `placeholderData: keepPreviousData`. Each term is cached under its own key. Consuming `signal` means a superseded search is aborted once its query goes inactive ([query cancellation](https://tanstack.com/query/v5/docs/framework/react/guides/query-cancellation)). The previous results stay on screen while the next ones load (D7). |
| `useTask(id)` | `taskKeys.detail(id)`. A 404 is not retried, and the page shows `NotFoundView`. |
| `useCreateTask()` | Not optimistic (spec). `onSuccess`: invalidate `taskKeys.lists()`. |
| `useUpdateTask(id)` | Detail save. Sends `ifMatch: baseVersion`. `onSuccess`: `setQueryData(detail)` and invalidate the lists. `onError` 412: invalidate the detail, so the newer version arrives and "Changed elsewhere" shows (§ 4.5). |
| `useToggleTask()` | Optimistic. **`onMutate`**: `await cancelQueries({ queryKey: taskKeys.all })`; snapshot with `getQueriesData`; `setQueriesData` flips `completed` in every list and the detail; return the snapshot. **`onError`**: 404 → remove the task from every cache entry and report "That task was deleted elsewhere." Anything else → restore the snapshot and report the failure. **`onSettled`**: invalidate the lists. No `If-Match`, because a toggle sets an absolute value (decision 9.7). |
| `useMoveTask()` | Optimistic, **`scope: { id: "task-order" }`**, so moves run one at a time, in order ([mutations: scopes](https://tanstack.com/query/v5/docs/framework/react/guides/mutations)). `onMutate`: `cancelQueries(taskKeys.lists())`, snapshot, then `setQueryData(taskKeys.list(""), items => moveAfter(items, id, afterId))`. `onError`: restore and report (404 → remove, as above). `onSettled`: invalidate the lists **only when `isMutating({ mutationKey: move }) === 1`**, so a refetch never lands between queued moves ([concurrent optimistic updates](https://tkdodo.eu/blog/concurrent-optimistic-updates-in-react-query)). |
| `useDeleteTask()` | Optimistic. `onMutate`: cancel, snapshot, remove from the lists, `removeQueries(detail)`. `onError`: 404 → keep it removed (it is gone either way); anything else → restore and report. `onSettled`: invalidate the lists. |
| `useTaskNotices()` | Derives the newest failed toggle, move or delete from `useMutationState({ filters: { mutationKey: ["tasks"], status: "error" } })`. Dismissal is local state (a set of dismissed `submittedAt` values). The list page shows notices from mutations started on the detail page, with no extra store. |
| `useMe()`, `useSignIn()`, `useSignUp()`, `useSignOut()` | `useMe` is `authKeys.me` with `staleTime: Infinity` (it changes only through these mutations). Sign-in and sign-up `setQueryData(authKeys.me, user)`. Sign-out clears the whole cache. |
| `useDebouncedValue(value, 250)` | A timer in `useEffect`, cleared on change. A timer is something outside React, so this is a legitimate effect. |

Pure helpers: `moveAfter(items: readonly Task[], id: string, afterId: string | null): readonly Task[]` uses `toSpliced` and `findIndex`, and returns a new array.

**One shared optimistic helper** (decision 9.24). Toggle, move and delete repeat the same four steps: cancel the list queries, snapshot them, apply a change to every cached list, and hand back the snapshot for rollback. One higher-order function holds them:

```ts
/** Build the onMutate step of an optimistic task-list update from a pure list transform. */
export const optimisticListUpdate = <V>(client: QueryClient, apply: (items: readonly Task[], vars: V) => readonly Task[]) =>
  async (vars: V): Promise<ListSnapshot> => …;   // cancelQueries, getQueriesData, setQueriesData(apply), return snapshot
export const restoreLists = (client: QueryClient, snapshot: ListSnapshot): void => …;
```

Each hook passes its own pure transform: `toggleIn(id, completed)` (a `map`), `moveAfter` (a `toSpliced`) or `removeFrom(id)` (a `filter`). Each hook keeps its own `onError`, because the three handle a 404 differently.

### 4.5 "Changed elsewhere" (D17)

The detail page keeps one piece of local state, `draft: { values: TaskDraft; baseVersion: number } | null`. `null` means not editing. Everything else is derived during render:

```ts
const isDirty = draft !== null && !isEqual(draft.values, draftFromTask(task));
const changedElsewhere = isChangedElsewhere(task, draft); // draft !== null && task.version > draft.baseVersion
```

- Editing starts on the first change, with `baseVersion = task.version` at that moment.
- A focus refetch that brings a newer version under a draft makes `changedElsewhere` true straight away. The draft is never overwritten.
- "Reload" sets `draft` to `null`. "Review" shows the newer values next to the draft, and from there "Keep mine" moves `baseVersion` to the current version **(Q-11)**.
- Save validates `draft.values` with `taskDraftSchema`, sends `diffDraft(task, draft)` (only the changed fields) with `If-Match: baseVersion`, and on success clears the draft. A 412 refetches, which turns the notice on.

### 4.6 Auth context, router, guard, error boundary, console

- **`AuthProvider`** exposes `{ status: "loading" | "signed-in" | "signed-out", user: User | null }`, derived from `useMe()` (never copied into state), plus `signIn`, `signUp` and `signOut` from the mutation hooks. `useAuth()` reads it.
- **Router** (`createAppRouter()`):

| Path | Element | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | `<Navigate to="/tasks" replace />` | |
| `/sign-in` | `SignInPage` | Signed in already → `/tasks` |
| `/sign-up` | `SignUpPage` | Signed in already → `/tasks` |
| layout | `RequireAuth` | `loading` → the shell's loading state; `signed-out` → `<Navigate to={"/sign-in?returnTo=" + path} replace />`; `signed-in` → `AppShell` around `<Outlet />` |
| `/tasks` | `TaskListPage` | |
| `/tasks/:taskId` | `TaskDetailPage` | A `taskId` that is not a UUID → `NotFoundView`, no request |
| `*` | `NotFoundPage` | |
| root `errorElement` | `RouteErrorPage` | Renders the design branch's `ErrorView` (message, "Try again", "Go to tasks") **(Q-12)** |

- **`returnTo`** is parsed with `returnToSchema`: it must start with `/` and not with `//`, otherwise `/tasks`. That blocks open redirects.
- **Console.** `main.tsx` logs `console.info("[app] started", { mode })` once. `RouteErrorPage` logs `console.error("[app] route error", error)`. The query caches log as in § 4.3. Nothing else logs.

### 4.7 Route containers and the props they supply

Each container is one file in `src/pages/`. It calls hooks and passes plain data and callbacks into one view. It renders no markup of its own beyond the view. Prop names below describe *what must be supplied*; the final names follow the views.

| Container | View | Must supply |
|---|---|---|
| `SignInPage` | `SignInView` | `onSubmit(credentials)`; `status: "idle" \| "submitting"`; `fieldErrors` (from `credentialsSchema`, or server `details`); `formError` for `invalid_credentials` and for network or 503 failures; the link to sign-up (keeping `returnTo`). On success → navigate to `returnTo`. |
| `SignUpPage` | `SignUpView` | As sign-in. `email_taken` (409) → field error on `email`. |
| `TaskListPage` | `TaskListView` | `state`: `loading` \| `error` (with `onRetry`) \| `ready` with `tasks`. `ready` with no tasks and no search is the **empty** state; with a search it is **no matches**. `searchTerm`, `onSearchChange`, `isSearching` (fetching while showing previous results). **`reorderEnabled = searchTerm.trim() === ""`**. `onMove(taskId, afterId \| null)`. `onToggle(taskId, completed)`. Quick add: `onCreate(title)`, `createStatus: "idle" \| "saving"`, `createFieldError`. The task link (href builder or `onOpen`). `notice` and `onDismissNotice` from `useTaskNotices`. |
| `TaskDetailPage` | `TaskDetailView` | `state`: `loading` \| `error` (with `onRetry`) \| `not-found` (renders `NotFoundView`) \| `ready`. `task` (server values), `draft` values and `onFieldChange(field, value)`, `fieldErrors`, `isDirty`, `saveStatus: "idle" \| "saving"`, `saveError`, `onSave`, `onCancel`. `changedElsewhere` with `onReview`, `onReload`, `onKeepMine` and the newer values for review. Delete: `onDelete` (the confirm step lives in the view per the spec, or as two callbacks if the view prefers). After delete → navigate to `/tasks`. |
| `NotFoundPage` | `NotFoundView` | The link back to `/tasks` |
| `RequireAuth` layout | `AppShell` | `user.email`, `onSignOut`, `signingOut` |

1075	
1076	**Retargeting a stacked child.** GitHub's squash-merge puts one new commit on the round branch. The branch stacked on it still carries the old ones. Once the parent child merges, the stacked branch is moved onto the round branch:
1077	
1078	```bash
1079	git fetch origin
1080	git rebase --onto origin/round/1-containers <old tip of the merged child> <stacked branch>
1081	git push --force-with-lease origin <stacked branch>   # asks first; the hook refuses force pushes only to main and round branches
1082	gh pr edit <n> --base round/1-containers
1083	```
1084	
1085	`<old tip of the merged child>` is the head SHA of the merged PR (`gh pr view <merged n> --json headRefOid`). After the rebase, the gates run again on the stacked branch before its PR goes back for review, because every commit on it is new.
1086	
1087	**External waits** (not agent time): about 2 minutes of CI per push; the lead's review of every PR, child and parent, and of every deployment artifact; first-time Docker image pulls and builds; Playwright's browser download in CI; the load runs themselves (about 5 minutes for the 200-user run and about 15 for the stepped run).

1157	## 9. Decisions this plan makes that the spec did not spell out
1158	
1159	| # | Decision | Reason |
1160	|---|---|---|
1161	| 9.1 | `rank_between` uses floor division for the midpoint digit | The spec's `a0F` example requires it; the reference implementation's rounding would give `a0G` |
1162	| 9.2 | The fractional-indexing key format (integer part plus fraction) | The spec's `a0` keys match it. New tasks go to the top, so prepending is the commonest insert, and the integer part keeps prepends to 2 or 3 characters instead of growing the key every few inserts. |
1163	| 9.3 | `notes` is `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` | One empty value, not two (`null` and `""`) |
1164	| 9.4 | The API strips the title's surrounding whitespace, and a check stops a blank title | A title of spaces is not a title. The design branch's `taskSchema` must `trim()` to match (sent to the designer). |
1165	| 9.5 | One `Credentials` model (12 to 128 characters) for login and register | It mirrors the single `credentialsSchema`. A short password at sign-in gets 400 rather than 401, which reveals only the public policy. |
1166	| 9.6 | A move changes only `rank`; `version` and `updatedAt` stay | The version guards the fields a person edits. Otherwise a reorder in one tab would trip "Changed elsewhere" in another. |
1167	| 9.7 | The list's toggle sends no `If-Match`; it bumps `version` | A toggle sets an absolute value, so last-write-wins is correct for it. The bump still warns a stale detail draft. |
1168	| 9.8 | An empty `PATCH` is 400 | Nothing to change is a client mistake, not a silent no-op that bumps the version |
1169	| 9.9 | Request models use `extra="forbid"`, and `completed` is `StrictBool`. No model-wide `strict=True`. | Typos (`after_id`) and boolean coercions (`"yes"` as true) fail as 400. Model-wide strict mode would also reject ISO dates and UUID strings, because FastAPI validates in Python mode (§ 3.6). |
1170	| 9.10 | Readiness relies on uvicorn closing its sockets at shutdown | uvicorn already refuses new connections before draining; a second flag would duplicate it |
1171	| 9.11 | Successful probes are left out of the access log | Two probes every 5 s per replica would bury the lines worth reading |
1172	| 9.12 | Sign-in with an unknown email still runs one dummy verify | Equal timing, so response time does not reveal which emails exist |
1173	| 9.13 | The Vite dev proxy rewrites `Origin` to `APP_ORIGIN` | `npm run dev` against the compose stack would otherwise get 403 on every write |
1174	| 9.14 | Pool numbers are settings with the locked defaults; timeouts and the JWT lifetime are constants | Tests need a tiny pool and round 3 may retune behind PgBouncer. Nothing varies the rest. |
1175	| 9.15 | Compose publishes `127.0.0.1:8080`, not every interface | The app is for this Mac, not the local network |
1176	| 9.16 | `Location` headers are relative | Correct behind any proxy without trusting forwarded headers |
1177	| 9.17 | `/api/` responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store` | Private data never sits in a shared or browser cache |
1178	| 9.18 | Search terms over 200 characters → 400 | No title is longer, and it bounds the trigram work |
1179	| 9.19 | Session tokens hold only `sub`, `iat` and `exp`; task routes never load the user | Stateless across replicas (D4); `/auth/me` is the one route that reads the row |
1180	| 9.20 | List notices come from `useMutationState`, not a new store | Server-side outcomes stay in TanStack Query, and the list sees failures from the detail page |
1181	| 9.21 | No `asyncio.TaskGroup` in app code in round 1 | No request has independent awaits to run together (sign-in's read and verify are sequential). `TaskGroup` drives the race tests. Adding one without a real need would be speculative. |
1182	| 9.22 | `UserRead` returns `id` and `email` only | It matches the design branch's `userSchema`; nothing on screen reads a creation time |
1183	| 9.23 | Load-test and e2e accounts use `@example.com` | email-validator refuses special-use domains such as `test`; `example.com` is reserved for documentation (RFC 2606) and accepted |
1184	| 9.24 | Toggle, move and delete share one higher-order helper, `optimisticListUpdate` | Three callers repeat the same cancel, snapshot, apply and rollback steps. One function with a pure transform per caller removes that repetition. With a single caller it would not exist. |
1185	| 9.25 | Dependencies are pinned exactly, and each PR re-checks the pins it introduces | § 13 is a snapshot of 2026-10-19. A pin that ages past a security fix is caught when its PR is raised, not after. |

1189	## 10. Risks
1190	
1191	| Risk | Effect | Mitigation |
1192	|---|---|---|
1193	| uvicorn's own 503 and nginx's 502 and 504 carry no envelope | A client that only reads the envelope crashes | The fetch wrapper's fallback (§ 4.2) and a unit test; Q-2 |
1194	| Idle nginx keep-alive connections count toward `--limit-concurrency` | Spurious 503s under load | `worker_processes 2` × `keepalive 16` = at most 32 idle connections in total, so at worst 32 of a replica's 200 slots (16 each when spread evenly). Unpinned, a 10-core Mac could hold 160. The load test watches for 503s. |
1195	| Load results depend on Docker Desktop's CPU and memory, and k6 shares the Mac | The capacity figure is not comparable across machines | Record Docker's resources with the results; quote them in the README |
1196	| Zod's `.max()` counts UTF-16 units, Python and Postgres count code points | A 200-emoji title passes the API but not the form | The form is stricter, never looser; documented, no fix in round 1 |
1197	| Swagger UI loads its files from a CDN | `/api/docs` breaks offline or under a strict CSP | A scoped CSP for that path; Q-13 |
1198	| `citext` and `pg_trgm` must be allowed on Azure Postgres | The round 3 migration fails | Both are on Azure's supported list for 17 and 18 ([extensions by engine](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/extensions/concepts-extensions-by-engine?pivots=postgresql-18)). Note for round 3: allow-list them in the `azure.extensions` server parameter. |
1199	| Pins age; new CVEs land after 2026-10-19 | A shipped image carries a known bug | Each PR re-checks its pins (decision 9.25); § 13 lists what to recheck |
1200	| `asgi-lifespan` 2.1.0 has had no release since 2023 | A future Starlette change could break test start-up | It speaks only the ASGI lifespan protocol. Fallback: enter `app.router.lifespan_context(app)` in the fixture. |
1201	| Debug-mode asyncio slows the backend suite | A longer CI step | Accepted. The guard is the point. |
1202	| `hashtextextended` can collide between two users | Two users' order writes occasionally queue together | Harmless (64-bit hash, a few milliseconds at worst) |
1203	| Rank length grows when many moves land in one gap | Longer keys | Bounded in tests; rebalancing is in `FUTURE.md` |
1204	| Browser fonts or styles from a CDN in the design branch | CSP blocks them | Sent to the designer: bundle fonts, no inline `<style>` |

1361	## 14. Functional style map
1362	
1363	`TASK.md` asks for "higher-order functions, function composition, correct use of basic data structures and manipulations (map, reduce, apply, etc.)" and async through high-level abstractions. The lead made these hard requirements. This table shows where each one lives and why it belongs there. It is what the instructions walkthrough uses, and what reviewers will probe. It lists only places where the construct earns its keep.
1364	
1365	| What `TASK.md` asks for | Backend: where, and why there | Frontend: where, and why there |
1366	|---|---|---|
1367	| Higher-order functions | `Depends(get_session, scope="function")`, `Depends(get_current_user)` and `Depends(require_trusted_origin)`: FastAPI takes these functions and composes each request from them, so settings, the session and the user reach a route without globals. `Hasher.hash` passes the hashing function to `asyncio.to_thread` behind a semaphore. The rank core passes predicates and step functions to `takewhile`, `reduce` and `all`. | `createQueryClient({ onUnauthenticated })` takes the redirect as a function, so the query client never imports the router. `queryFn: ({ signal }) => listTasks(q, signal)`, `retry: (count, error) => …` and `setQueriesData(key, updater)` are all functions handed to TanStack. `optimisticListUpdate(client, apply)` (§ 4.4) builds the shared `onMutate` for toggle, move and delete: three callers, so it removes real repetition. |
1368	| Function composition | A request flows middleware → dependencies → router → service → repository, each a small function the next one calls. `search_pattern(normalize_query(q))`. `rank_between` is built from `split_rank`, `increment` or `decrement`, and `midpoint`. Python has no compose operator and nesting small functions is the idiom, so there is no `compose()` helper. | `apiRequest` is `fetch`, then a status check, then `schema.parse` (or `errorEnvelopeSchema.safeParse` into an `ApiError`). Each page container composes hooks into props for one view. A save runs `diffDraft`, then `taskPatchSchema.parse`, then `updateTask`. |
1369	| Correct data structures | `STATUS_BY_ERROR: Mapping[type[DomainError], tuple[int, str]]`: one handler finds any error's status in O(1), and reviewers check one table. `DIGIT_VALUE` (a read-only mapping, not `str.index`), `DIGIT_SET` (a frozenset, for membership) and `RANK_RULES` (a tuple: fixed and ordered). `TaskChanges` is a `TypedDict` for a partial update. In Postgres, the unique index on `(owner_id, rank)` is both the ordered access path and the uniqueness guard, and `citext` makes email equality case-insensitive inside the index itself. | Query keys are hierarchical tuples, so `invalidateQueries(taskKeys.lists())` reaches every cached search at once. `ApiErrorCode` is an `as const` object: a closed set with an exhaustive `switch`. Dismissed notices are a `ReadonlySet` (membership). Task lists stay arrays because order is the point. |
1370	| map, filter, reduce, apply | `apply_patch` is a dict comprehension over `dataclasses.fields(patch)` that filters out `UNSET`. Validation `details` come from a list comprehension over Pydantic's errors. `reduce` carries the carry in `step_digits`. "Apply" here is function application: `to_thread(fn, *args)`, and FastAPI calling the dependency functions. | Toggle: `items.map(t => t.id === id ? { ...t, completed } : t)`. Delete: `items.filter(t => t.id !== id)`. Notices: `filter` to failed mutations, then `reduce` to the newest. `moveAfter`: `findIndex`, then `toSpliced`. Server field errors: `Object.fromEntries(details.map(d => [d.field, d.message]))`. |
1371	| Immutability | Frozen Pydantic models (`frozen=True`), frozen dataclasses (`TaskPatch`, `SessionClaims`, `Hasher`), tuples for fixed data and `MappingProxyType` for `DIGIT_VALUE`. No function mutates its input, and the rank functions build new strings. | `readonly` types, and `toSpliced`, `with` and spread instead of `splice`, `sort` or assignment. Cache updaters return new arrays, which TanStack's structural sharing depends on. The draft is replaced, never edited in place. |
1372	| Declarative over imperative | `match (lower, upper)` in `rank_between`. Guards declared in SQL (unique indexes, `CHECK`s) rather than checked in Python. The error map as data. | The router as a route table, the Zod schemas that forms validate against, and the k6 budgets as threshold data. |
1373	| Async through high-level abstractions | Async SQLAlchemy sessions with `async with session.begin()`, `asyncio.to_thread` with `asyncio.Semaphore`, `asyncio.timeout` in `/readyz`, logging through a `QueueHandler` thread, and `asyncio.TaskGroup` in the race tests | TanStack Query for every request: caching, cancellation through `AbortSignal`, optimistic updates with rollback, and a mutation `scope` that runs reorders one at a time. Never `useEffect` plus `fetch`. |
1374	
1375	**Where we deliberately don't**, so the walkthrough can say why:
1376	
1377	- No generic `compose` or `pipe` helper, no currying and no decorators of our own. Each would add a concept without removing any repetition.
1378	- No `functools.partial` where a direct call reads as well.
1379	- `midpoint` recurses instead of folding, and `rank_between` dispatches with `match` instead of a table of functions. § 3.7.1 says why.
1380	- No `TaskGroup` in app code (decision 9.21).
1381	- No loops are expected in app code. If one appears, it must read more clearly than the expression it replaces (`coding-standards.md`).

## 8. Delivery sequence

### 8.1 One parent PR, child PRs into the round branch

This follows `CONTRIBUTING.md` § 1 and `git-and-prs.md`. The lead reviews every PR, child and parent alike.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Round branch** | `round/1-containers`. The human creates it once from `main` (`git push origin main:refs/heads/round/1-containers`); the hook refuses that push from an agent. It is protected like `main`: no direct commits or pushes, only merged PRs. |
| **Parent PR** | `round/1-containers` → `main`, titled `feat(round-1): run the to do app in containers`, label `round`. It is opened as a draft once S1 has merged into the round branch. It links every child PR and serves as the round's checklist. It stays a draft until G5. After the human lead's final review it is **rebase-merged**, which lays the round's child commits onto `main` in order: `main` stays linear, one commit per child PR. |
| **Child PRs** | Each targets `round/1-containers`, or, while stacked, the branch of the unmerged child it builds on. Each is **squash-merged**: one commit on the round branch, its subject the PR title (Conventional, checked by the hook and CI). The PR keeps the green, test-first commits for review. |

| Order | PR | Branch | Contents | Base when raised → once its parent child merges | Label | Gate before merge | Size (bounded work) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

B and Cf touch disjoint folders, so either can be reviewed first once A has merged.

**Retargeting a stacked child.** GitHub's squash-merge puts one new commit on the round branch. The branch stacked on it still carries the old ones. Once the parent child merges, the stacked branch is moved onto the round branch:

```bash
git fetch origin
git rebase --onto origin/round/1-containers <old tip of the merged child> <stacked branch>
git push --force-with-lease origin <stacked branch>   # asks first; the hook refuses force pushes only to main and round branches
gh pr edit <n> --base round/1-containers
```

`<old tip of the merged child>` is the head SHA of the merged PR (`gh pr view <merged n> --json headRefOid`). After the rebase, the gates run again on the stacked branch before its PR goes back for review, because every commit on it is new.

**External waits** (not agent time): about 2 minutes of CI per push; the lead's review of every PR, child and parent, and of every deployment artifact; first-time Docker image pulls and builds; Playwright's browser download in CI; the load runs themselves (about 5 minutes for the 200-user run and about 15 for the stepped run).

## 9. Decisions this plan makes that the spec did not spell out

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 9.1 | `rank_between` uses floor division for the midpoint digit | The spec's `a0F` example requires it; the reference implementation's rounding would give `a0G` |
| 9.2 | The fractional-indexing key format (integer part plus fraction) | The spec's `a0` keys match it. New tasks go to the top, so prepending is the commonest insert, and the integer part keeps prepends to 2 or 3 characters instead of growing the key every few inserts. |
| 9.3 | `notes` is `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` | One empty value, not two (`null` and `""`) |
| 9.4 | The API strips the title's surrounding whitespace, and a check stops a blank title | A title of spaces is not a title. The design branch's `taskSchema` must `trim()` to match (sent to the designer). |
| 9.5 | One `Credentials` model (12 to 128 characters) for login and register | It mirrors the single `credentialsSchema`. A short password at sign-in gets 400 rather than 401, which reveals only the public policy. |
| 9.6 | A move changes only `rank`; `version` and `updatedAt` stay | The version guards the fields a person edits. Otherwise a reorder in one tab would trip "Changed elsewhere" in another. |
| 9.7 | The list's toggle sends no `If-Match`; it bumps `version` | A toggle sets an absolute value, so last-write-wins is correct for it. The bump still warns a stale detail draft. |
| 9.8 | An empty `PATCH` is 400 | Nothing to change is a client mistake, not a silent no-op that bumps the version |
| 9.9 | Request models use `extra="forbid"`, and `completed` is `StrictBool`. No model-wide `strict=True`. | Typos (`after_id`) and boolean coercions (`"yes"` as true) fail as 400. Model-wide strict mode would also reject ISO dates and UUID strings, because FastAPI validates in Python mode (§ 3.6). |
| 9.10 | Readiness relies on uvicorn closing its sockets at shutdown | uvicorn already refuses new connections before draining; a second flag would duplicate it |
| 9.11 | Successful probes are left out of the access log | Two probes every 5 s per replica would bury the lines worth reading |
| 9.12 | Sign-in with an unknown email still runs one dummy verify | Equal timing, so response time does not reveal which emails exist |
| 9.13 | The Vite dev proxy rewrites `Origin` to `APP_ORIGIN` | `npm run dev` against the compose stack would otherwise get 403 on every write |
| 9.14 | Pool numbers are settings with the locked defaults; timeouts and the JWT lifetime are constants | Tests need a tiny pool and round 3 may retune behind PgBouncer. Nothing varies the rest. |
| 9.15 | Compose publishes `127.0.0.1:8080`, not every interface | The app is for this Mac, not the local network |
| 9.16 | `Location` headers are relative | Correct behind any proxy without trusting forwarded headers |
| 9.17 | `/api/` responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store` | Private data never sits in a shared or browser cache |
| 9.18 | Search terms over 200 characters → 400 | No title is longer, and it bounds the trigram work |
| 9.19 | Session tokens hold only `sub`, `iat` and `exp`; task routes never load the user | Stateless across replicas (D4); `/auth/me` is the one route that reads the row |
| 9.20 | List notices come from `useMutationState`, not a new store | Server-side outcomes stay in TanStack Query, and the list sees failures from the detail page |
| 9.21 | No `asyncio.TaskGroup` in app code in round 1 | No request has independent awaits to run together (sign-in's read and verify are sequential). `TaskGroup` drives the race tests. Adding one without a real need would be speculative. |
| 9.22 | `UserRead` returns `id` and `email` only | It matches the design branch's `userSchema`; nothing on screen reads a creation time |
| 9.23 | Load-test and e2e accounts use `@example.com` | email-validator refuses special-use domains such as `test`; `example.com` is reserved for documentation (RFC 2606) and accepted |
| 9.24 | Toggle, move and delete share one higher-order helper, `optimisticListUpdate` | Three callers repeat the same cancel, snapshot, apply and rollback steps. One function with a pure transform per caller removes that repetition. With a single caller it would not exist. |
| 9.25 | Dependencies are pinned exactly, and each PR re-checks the pins it introduces | § 13 is a snapshot of 2026-10-19. A pin that ages past a security fix is caught when its PR is raised, not after. |

---

## 10. Risks

| Risk | Effect | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| uvicorn's own 503 and nginx's 502 and 504 carry no envelope | A client that only reads the envelope crashes | The fetch wrapper's fallback (§ 4.2) and a unit test; Q-2 |
| Idle nginx keep-alive connections count toward `--limit-concurrency` | Spurious 503s under load | `worker_processes 2` × `keepalive 16` = at most 32 idle connections in total, so at worst 32 of a replica's 200 slots (16 each when spread evenly). Unpinned, a 10-core Mac could hold 160. The load test watches for 503s. |
| Load results depend on Docker Desktop's CPU and memory, and k6 shares the Mac | The capacity figure is not comparable across machines | Record Docker's resources with the results; quote them in the README |
| Zod's `.max()` counts UTF-16 units, Python and Postgres count code points | A 200-emoji title passes the API but not the form | The form is stricter, never looser; documented, no fix in round 1 |
| Swagger UI loads its files from a CDN | `/api/docs` breaks offline or under a strict CSP | A scoped CSP for that path; Q-13 |
| `citext` and `pg_trgm` must be allowed on Azure Postgres | The round 3 migration fails | Both are on Azure's supported list for 17 and 18 ([extensions by engine](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/extensions/concepts-extensions-by-engine?pivots=postgresql-18)). Note for round 3: allow-list them in the `azure.extensions` server parameter. |
| Pins age; new CVEs land after 2026-10-19 | A shipped image carries a known bug | Each PR re-checks its pins (decision 9.25); § 13 lists what to recheck |
| `asgi-lifespan` 2.1.0 has had no release since 2023 | A future Starlette change could break test start-up | It speaks only the ASGI lifespan protocol. Fallback: enter `app.router.lifespan_context(app)` in the fixture. |
| Debug-mode asyncio slows the backend suite | A longer CI step | Accepted. The guard is the point. |
| `hashtextextended` can collide between two users | Two users' order writes occasionally queue together | Harmless (64-bit hash, a few milliseconds at worst) |
| Rank length grows when many moves land in one gap | Longer keys | Bounded in tests; rebalancing is in `FUTURE.md` |
| Browser fonts or styles from a CDN in the design branch | CSP blocks them | Sent to the designer: bundle fonts, no inline `<style>` |

---

## 11. Open questions (each with a recommendation)

The lead locked all eighteen on 2026-10-19 as recommended. Q-1 to Q-13 keep the tech lead's notes, and the decisions are recorded word for word in kickoff § 5d. The plan body follows each answer.

| # | Question | Recommendation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q-1 | The spec writes the move body as `{"after_id": …}`, but `api-contract.md` and the kickoff lock camelCase on the wire | **`afterId`**, per the later and more specific rule. Fix the spec's caption and prose in its next revision. | Locked by the lead, 2026-10-19 |
| Q-2 | The spec says a 503 always carries the envelope, but uvicorn's `--limit-concurrency` reply is plain text and cannot | Keep the locked flag. The fetch wrapper maps any non-envelope 502, 503 or 504 to `service_unavailable`. Correct the spec's wording. (Intercepting in nginx would not carry over to round 2's ingress.) | Locked by the lead, 2026-10-19 |
| Q-3 | A write with **no** `Origin` header: allow or 403? | **Allow.** Browsers always send `Origin` on writes, so its absence means a script, which cannot carry a victim's cookie. Reject a mismatch and the literal `null`. Reviewers' bulk scripts then work without extra headers. | Locked by the lead, 2026-10-19 |
| Q-4 | `python.md` says the transaction comes from a dependency. This plan has the dependency give the session and the service open the transaction. | **Service-owned `session.begin()`.** Sign-in must not hold a pooled connection while it waits for a hash slot, and the advisory lock should sit visibly at the top of its transaction. Update `python.md` in PR C's docs check. | Locked by the lead, 2026-10-19 |
| Q-5 | Local backend tests need a Postgres the host can reach, but the spec says only :8080 is published | A `test-db` service under the `test` profile on `127.0.0.1:55432`, on tmpfs, off by default. The main stack still publishes only :8080. | Locked by the lead, 2026-10-19 |
| Q-6 | Should `.env.example` hold working local values, so a clean Mac needs only `cp .env.example .env`? | **Yes**, labelled local-only, with the `openssl` lines for real use | Locked by the lead, 2026-10-19 (tech lead's note: provided the app refuses to start with the example `JWT_SECRET` unless `COOKIE_SECURE=false` (now in § 3.1, tested in § 6.2)) |
| Q-7 | The spec plans one backend PR. At about 45 files it is a long line-by-line read. | Split into `feature/api-foundation` (C1 to C8) and `feature/api-tasks` (C9 to C14, including CP1). The commit sequence is the same either way. | Locked by the lead, 2026-10-19 (tech lead's note: split) |
| Q-8 | The spec names `apply_patch` in the core. ## 14. Functional style map

`TASK.md` asks for "higher-order functions, function composition, correct use of basic data structures and manipulations (map, reduce, apply, etc.)" and async through high-level abstractions. The lead made these hard requirements. This table shows where each one lives and why it belongs there. It is what the instructions walkthrough uses, and what reviewers will probe. It lists only places where the construct earns its keep.

| What `TASK.md` asks for | Backend: where, and why there | Frontend: where, and why there |
|---|---|---|
| Higher-order functions | `Depends(get_session, scope="function")`, `Depends(get_current_user)` and `Depends(require_trusted_origin)`: FastAPI takes these functions and composes each request from them, so settings, the session and the user reach a route without globals. `Hasher.hash` passes the hashing function to `asyncio.to_thread` behind a semaphore. The rank core passes predicates and step functions to `takewhile`, `reduce` and `all`. | `createQueryClient({ onUnauthenticated })` takes the redirect as a function, so the query client never imports the router. `queryFn: ({ signal }) => listTasks(q, signal)`, `retry: (count, error) => …` and `setQueriesData(key, updater)` are all functions handed to TanStack. `optimisticListUpdate(client, apply)` (§ 4.4) builds the shared `onMutate` for toggle, move and delete: three callers, so it removes real repetition. |
| Function composition | A request flows middleware → dependencies → router → service → repository, each a small function the next one calls. `search_pattern(normalize_query(q))`. `rank_between` is built from `split_rank`, `increment` or `decrement`, and `midpoint`. Python has no compose operator and nesting small functions is the idiom, so there is no `compose()` helper. | `apiRequest` is `fetch`, then a status check, then `schema.parse` (or `errorEnvelopeSchema.safeParse` into an `ApiError`). Each page container composes hooks into props for one view. A save runs `diffDraft`, then `taskPatchSchema.parse`, then `updateTask`. |
| Correct data structures | `STATUS_BY_ERROR: Mapping[type[DomainError], tuple[int, str]]`: one handler finds any error's status in O(1), and reviewers check one table. `DIGIT_VALUE` (a read-only mapping, not `str.index`), `DIGIT_SET` (a frozenset, for membership) and `RANK_RULES` (a tuple: fixed and ordered). `TaskChanges` is a `TypedDict` for a partial update. In Postgres, the unique index on `(owner_id, rank)` is both the ordered access path and the uniqueness guard, and `citext` makes email equality case-insensitive inside the index itself. | Query keys are hierarchical tuples, so `invalidateQueries(taskKeys.lists())` reaches every cached search at once. `ApiErrorCode` is an `as const` object: a closed set with an exhaustive `switch`. Dismissed notices are a `ReadonlySet` (membership). Task lists stay arrays because order is the point. |
| map, filter, reduce, apply | `apply_patch` is a dict comprehension over `dataclasses.fields(patch)` that filters out `UNSET`. Validation `details` come from a list comprehension over Pydantic's errors. `reduce` carries the carry in `step_digits`. "Apply" here is function application: `to_thread(fn, *args)`, and FastAPI calling the dependency functions. | Toggle: `items.map(t => t.id === id ? { ...t, completed } : t)`. Delete: `items.filter(t => t.id !== id)`. Notices: `filter` to failed mutations, then `reduce` to the newest. `moveAfter`: `findIndex`, then `toSpliced`. Server field errors: `Object.fromEntries(details.map(d => [d.field, d.message]))`. |
| Immutability | Frozen Pydantic models (`frozen=True`), frozen dataclasses (`TaskPatch`, `SessionClaims`, `Hasher`), tuples for fixed data and `MappingProxyType` for `DIGIT_VALUE`. No function mutates its input, and the rank functions build new strings. | `readonly` types, and `toSpliced`, `with` and spread instead of `splice`, `sort` or assignment. Cache updaters return new arrays, which TanStack's structural sharing depends on. The draft is replaced, never edited in place. |

# Python

## Boundaries and types
- Pydantic models at every boundary: request and response bodies, database rows leaving the repository layer, token claims. `Model.model_validate(raw)` right after deserializing; field access happens on the model.
- Request and response models are separate types (`TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate`, `TaskRead`). A response never exposes a column the client should not see, such as a password hash.
- Settings are one pydantic-settings class. With `extra="ignore"` a typo in an env var name fails silently, so check the name when a value is missing.
- `X | None` and `dict[str, X]`. `Mapping` and `Sequence` for parameters you only read. A frozen dataclass or TypedDict for a value that stays inside the service; a Pydantic model for anything that crosses a boundary.
- `uv run mypy` runs in strict mode and passes.

## Docstrings
- Google style: a summary line in the imperative, a blank line, then `Args:`, `Returns:`, `Raises:` as needed. Types stay in the hints, never repeated in the docstring. Private helpers and tests need only the summary line, and only when the name does not already say it.

## FastAPI
- Routers stay thin: parse, call the service or core, map the result to a response model. No SQL and no business rules in a router.
- Dependencies (`Depends`) compose the request: settings, session, current user. Ownership is enforced in the query (`WHERE owner_id = :user_id`), not by loading a row and checking it afterwards.
- Domain errors are exceptions raised by the service and turned into HTTP responses by one set of exception handlers in the app factory. Handlers never build error bodies by hand. The status code contract is in `api-contract.md`.
- Build the app in a factory (`create_app(settings)`) so tests build their own app with their own settings.

## Failure handling and logging
- On a validation error at a boundary: log at WARNING with the function name, the error, and a sanitized snippet, then take the documented fail-soft path. Never silent.
- `log = logging.getLogger(__name__)`. No `print`. The root logger is configured once, in the app factory, before any request is served.
- WARNING and ERROR lines say where (`module.function`), why, and what happens next, with ids as key=value. Never log secrets.

## Async and boot
- asyncio throughout. Every route is `async def`; a plain `def` route would run on FastAPI's thread pool. Do not block the event loop: no sync database driver, no sync HTTP client, no blocking file I/O on the request path.
- CPU-heavy work runs through `asyncio.to_thread` behind a semaphore that caps it per process. Password hashing (argon2id, OWASP parameters) is capped at 4 at a time.
- One `AsyncSession` per request, from a dependency declared with `scope="function"` so it closes before the response is sent. Each service opens its one transaction with `async with session.begin()`: it commits before the router builds the response and rolls back on any exception. CPU work such as password hashing runs outside the transaction, so it never holds a pooled connection. Never share a session between concurrent coroutines; a `TaskGroup` that touches the database gives each task its own session.
- Logging goes through a `QueueHandler` so a slow stdout never blocks the loop.
- Never add a network call at import time; put it in the lifespan. A database the app cannot reach makes `/readyz` fail, not the import.
---

  - "frontend/src/**/*.ts"
  - "frontend/src/**/*.tsx"
---
# TypeScript

- `strict` is on in `tsconfig.json`. No `any`, no `as unknown as`, no `@ts-ignore`, no non-null `!` to silence a real `undefined`. Named exports. Function components with hooks; no classes, except `Error` subclasses (`ApiError`), which `instanceof` narrowing and TanStack Query's typed errors need.
- Every boundary is a Zod schema under `src/lib/schema/`: API responses, form data, storage, URL params. `parse`, or `safeParse` with a typed error path, right after reading; field access on the parsed value. Types come from the schema with `z.infer`, never written twice.
- Every API call goes through the one fetch wrapper in `src/lib/api/`, which sends the session cookie (same origin), parses the body and turns error bodies into a typed `ApiError`. No bare `fetch` in components or hooks.
- Domain types live in `src/types/` or next to their schema, reachable from any layer. Never define a cross-cutting type inside `components/`.
- Enums are `as const` objects, not `enum`. Use the typed constant, never the string literal.
- Discriminated unions are closed. Switch on the discriminant, and make the switch exhaustive with a `never` check.
- Environment values are read through one module, never raw `import.meta.env` in components. Build-time values are public; a secret never goes there.
- JSDoc: a summary line on every exported function, component and type. `@param` and `@returns` only when they say something the signature does not.
- Logic lives in exported pure helpers a test can reach (filtering, ordering, formatting), not inline in markup.
- Filenames are kebab-case. Tests sit next to the code they test as `<name>.test.ts(x)`.
- `npm run check` (ESLint, Prettier check, `tsc --noEmit`) is the gate.

# API contract

The REST contract between `backend/` and `frontend/`. Change both sides in the same PR, or neither.

- Resources are nouns under `/api/v1`: `/auth/...`, `/tasks`, `/tasks/{id}`. Standard methods: `GET` reads, `POST` creates, `PATCH` updates part of a resource, `DELETE` removes. A move is `PUT /tasks/{id}/position` with `{"afterId": ...}`: the task goes right after that task, or to the top when it is null. JSON in and out.
- Status codes:

| Case | Code |
|---|---|
| Read or update succeeded | 200 |
| Created; the response carries the resource and a `Location` header | 201 |
| Deleted | 204, no body |
| Body, query or `If-Match` header fails validation, or a move's `afterId` is not one of the user's other tasks | **400** (FastAPI's default is 422; the app maps `RequestValidationError` to 400 in one handler) |
| No token, bad token, expired token, wrong password | 401 |
| Authenticated but not allowed to do this action | 403 |
| Resource missing, **or owned by another user** (so ids of other users' tasks are never confirmed) | 404 |
| Conflict with current state, such as an email already registered | 409 |
| `If-Match` names an old version of the task | 412 |
| Overloaded (in-flight limit, no free database connection) or database unreachable | 503 |
| Any other HTTP-level error the framework raises (for example 415): the envelope with code `http_error` and the original status | as raised |

- JSON field names are camelCase on the wire (`dueDate`, `createdAt`). Pydantic models use `alias_generator=to_camel` with `populate_by_name=True`; Python code keeps snake_case.
- Tasks carry an integer `version`, returned as the `ETag` header as a quoted number (`"3"`). `PATCH` honours `If-Match` (412 on mismatch) and changes only the fields sent; without `If-Match` it always applies. Every edit bumps the version; a move does not.
- Every error body has one shape, a typed model: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "details": [...]}}`. `code` is a stable machine string the frontend switches on; `message` is safe to show a user.
- List endpoints return a typed envelope, not a bare array, so paging can be added without breaking clients.
- The frontend parses every response with a Zod schema that mirrors the backend's Pydantic model. When a model changes, the schema changes in the same PR, and the integration test for that endpoint asserts the new shape.
- Every endpoint has an integration test for its success code and each error code it can return.

# Contributing to `todo-app`

This file is the canonical reference for *how* we work in this repo. The *why* (requirements, architecture, design decisions) lives in `docs/`: start with `docs/kickoff.md`.

> **TL;DR for first-time contributors:** branch off the current round branch (`round/<n>-<name>`), use Conventional Commits, run the tests before opening a PR into the round branch, get the human lead's review. The round reaches `main` in one parent PR once it is done and tested.

---

## 1. Branches and merges

Work is organised in rounds (round 1: containers, round 2: local k3d, round 3: AKS). Each round has one integration branch and one parent PR.

```
feature/<name>              ←  you work here, branched off the round branch
       │
       │  GATE — every suite passes on this branch (§ 5)
       ▼
  child PR  →  round/<n>-<name>   ←  reviewed by the human lead, then squash-merged
       │                             (one commit per child PR, titled by the PR)
       │  GATE — the round is done: exit criteria met, every suite green
       ▼
 parent PR  →  main              ←  open (as a draft) for the whole round;
       │                             rebase-merged once tested (one commit per child on main)
       ▼
   vX.Y.Z tag                    ←  a release is a tag on main; a tag is never moved or deleted
```

- **The parent PR** is opened as a draft as soon as the round branch has its first merged child, and is titled for the round (`feat(round-1): run the to do app in containers`). It is the round's checklist: each child PR is linked from it. It leaves draft only when the round's exit criteria are met, and it merges only after the human lead's final review.
- **`main` only ever receives finished, tested rounds.** Rebase-merging the parent lays the round's child commits onto `main` in order, so `main` stays linear with one commit per child PR. Each child's test-first commits stay visible in its merged PR on GitHub.
- **Child PRs** target the round branch and are squash-merged, so the PR title becomes the commit subject (the PR-title hook and CI keep it Conventional). Every commit on the PR branch is still green, and the test-first order stays in the PR. A child that depends on an unmerged child targets that child's branch until it merges, then is rebased onto the round branch (`git rebase --onto origin/round/<n>-<name> <old tip of the merged child>`) and retargeted.
- **After the parent PR is rebase-merged,** `main` holds the round's commits under new IDs, so the round branch is deleted and the next round's branch is created from `main`.

# backend

The REST API: FastAPI on Python 3.14, async SQLAlchemy with asyncpg, alembic migrations, Postgres 18. Today it serves the health probes, sign-up, sign-in, sign-out and the current user, and the signed-in user's tasks: create, read, list, search, edit, move and delete.

## Commands

Run from `backend/` unless noted.

```bash
uv sync                                    # Python 3.14.8 and the locked dependencies
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check . && uv run mypy && uv run pytest   # the gate; every commit passes it
HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=ci uv run pytest        # 1,000 examples per property, as CI runs them (200 by default)
uv run pytest tests/integration/test_races.py --no-cov   # one file alone; without --no-cov the 90% floor fails it
DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://... uv run alembic upgrade head   # apply migrations; `downgrade base` undoes them
```

The integration tests need a Postgres. From the repo root:

```bash
docker compose --profile test up -d --wait test-db    # throwaway server on 127.0.0.1:55432, data in memory
docker compose --profile test down                    # stop and remove it
```

Compose reads every service's variables, so even `test-db` needs a `.env` in the repo root. The human creates it once with `cp .env.example .env`. The suite drops and rebuilds its own `todo_test` database from the migrations on each run, and empties both tables before each test. Set `TEST_DATABASE_URL` to point it at another server's maintenance database (CI does).

Coverage below 90% fails the run. Unit tests never open a socket; integration tests run against the real database.

## Config

# frontend

React 19 SPA in TypeScript (Vite 8, React Router 8, TanStack Query 5, Tailwind 4, Zod 4, dnd-kit). Views take props and render; a container per route in `src/pages/` feeds each view from TanStack Query.

## Commands

```bash
npm ci                       # Node 24
npm run dev                  # the app on Vite's dev server
npm run check                # ESLint (type-checked) + prettier --check + tsc --noEmit
npm run test                 # Vitest + coverage; fails under 85% lines, branches, functions or statements
npm run build                # tsc, then the app into dist/
npm run design:dev           # the design gallery on Vite's dev server
npm run design:build         # the gallery as one self-contained file: design/dist/artifact.html
npm run design:screenshots   # after design:build; needs `npx playwright install chromium` once
```

Every commit passes `check`, `test` and `build`.

## Layout

- `src/main.tsx`: boot. One query client, the router, and the `[app] started` line.
- `src/app/`: the route table and the ended-session redirect (`router.tsx`), the signed-in guard (`require-auth.tsx`), and the route error boundary (`route-error.tsx`).
- `src/pages/`: one container per route. Hooks in, one view out, no markup of its own.
- `src/styles/tokens.css`: every colour, size, radius, shadow and duration, as Tailwind `@theme` tokens. The default theme is cleared, so a utility off the scale (`p-5`, `bg-red-500`) does not exist.
- `src/styles/index.css`: Tailwind, fonts, the `binding` and `ruled` utilities, and the hover, focus-visible and active variants the gallery can force.
- `src/components/ui/`: primitives. `src/components/`: compositions (`AppShell`, `AuthLayout`, `CredentialsForm`).
- `src/views/`: one view per screen. Props in, JSX out: no fetching, no router hooks, every intent leaves as a callback. Only local affordances (a draft, an open confirm) live in `useState`.
- `src/lib/api/`: the fetch wrapper (`apiRequest`, `ApiError` with a closed set of codes) and one function per endpoint. Every request goes through it.
- `src/lib/query/`: query keys, the query client (the one place a 401 is handled), and the hooks for auth and tasks. Toggle, move and delete share `optimisticListUpdate`.
- `src/lib/auth/auth-context.tsx`: `useAuth`, the session and the sign-in, sign-up and sign-out actions.
- `src/lib/`: pure helpers (`tasks/order.ts`, `task-draft.ts`, `task-list.ts`, `due-date.ts`), `routes.ts` with `signInPath`, and `schema/` (Zod, shared by forms and the API layer, URL params included).
- `src/hooks/`: `useDebouncedValue`.
- `src/test/fixtures.ts`: the sample data and view props that both the tests and the gallery use.
- `src/test/server.ts`, `handlers.ts`: MSW at the `fetch` boundary, answering from the fixtures. `render-app.tsx` renders the whole app at a path, wired like `main.tsx`.
- `design/`: the gallery, a second Vite entry. `screens.tsx` lists every state; `Scripted` drives a view the way a user would to reach states held in local state. `screenshots/` is committed.

- Layout responds to container width (`@wide:`), not the viewport. A view needs an `@container` ancestor; `Page`, `AppShell` and `AuthLayout` provide one.
- The gallery build roots Vite at `design/`, so `index.css` names `src/` and `design/` as Tailwind sources explicitly.
- Vitest stubs CSS imports; only `tokens.css` is processed, so the token tests can read it.
- `data-hover`, `data-focus-visible` and `data-active` exist for the gallery only. Never set them in app code.
- The design build inlines everything; the app build must not inline anything (the nginx CSP is `'self'` only).
